Licence is 'to use a Deliverable' only; no modification right
14.2 states no purpose scope: 'licence to use a Deliverable'

reasons: Single targeted replacement of 14.2 flips ownership to Customer with an express assignment and converts the revocable, term-limited licence into a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence extending to embedded Vendor IP — all preferred elements are met.

Sections 14.1, 14.3 and 14.4 are untouched, so Customer Data ownership, Vendor's retained pre-existing technology and the no-joint-ownership bar remain effective; no dangling cross-reference is created (the 13.2 perpetual licence reference is preserved as drafted).

Correctly avoids importing fallback-only rights (worldwide, modify, sublicense), so the two bargains are not mixed; the fallback consequently fails on those elements, which is expected at the locked preferred target.

Minor, not a deviation: the retained licence 'to use a Deliverable' is now partly redundant of Customer's ownership, and 'Vendor IP' is a descriptive phrase rather than the defined 'Vendor Technology' — neither weakens Customer's position or creates a contradiction.
